sections.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
sections.abstract: How can a protein-binding RNA structure be generated without specifying its binding site or relative pose?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a structure-first pipeline that proposes protein interfaces, generates RNA conformations in a pretrained RNA latent space, predicts cross-frame interaction constraints, and places the RNA as a rigid body. On a temporally split, sequence-filtered benchmark of 124 complexes, they report the best fNAT and DockQ and lowest interface/ligand RMSDs among compared methods; native interface correspondence is used only post hoc.
sections.unique_caveat: Structural-computational evidence, not experimental binding or function. The authors identify interface-hypothesis ranking and sequence realization as unresolved.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations at snapshot; cross-listed from cs.LG into q-bio.BM, directly linking structure generation to molecular biology.

sections.title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
sections.abstract: Which single-cell RNA-seq synthesis choices preserve biological structure while limiting donor-membership leakage?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors compare scGFT, scLDM and Cell2Sentence on donor-split OneK1K data across fidelity, biological preservation and membership-inference risk. They report severe leakage when non-HVG values are copied, lower leakage with Poisson reconstruction, and near-random membership-inference profiles for tuned scGFT/scLDM configurations.
sections.unique_caveat: Generative modeling focuses on highly variable genes and reconstructs non-HVGs, reflecting stated time/computational limits. One dataset and empirical membership inference do not establish formal differential privacy or generalization.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; q-bio.GN paper whose arXiv comment notes presentation at the CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge.

sections.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
sections.abstract: How does DNA torsional stress alter protein-mediated condensation and genome compaction?
sections.claimed_contribution: Using a coupled DNA-elasticity/protein-concentration model and simulations, the authors propose that protein wetting promotes twist-to-writhe conversion, lowering the barrier to DNA–protein co-condensation under sufficient supercoiling.
sections.unique_caveat: The mechanism is theoretical/model-based, not an experimental demonstration in cells. Predictions depend on model parameters and require validation across relevant proteins and chromatin contexts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; cross-listed in q-bio.BM, physics.bio-ph and cond-mat.soft.

sections.title: Shorter but not more catalytic: an active-site-resolved model of how tau reshapes amyloid-$β$ secondary nucleation
sections.abstract: Does tau-induced shortening of amyloid-β fibrils necessarily increase secondary-nucleation activity?
sections.claimed_contribution: The author extends a tau–amyloid-β kinetic model to track fibril number, mass and exposed catalytic sites. Simulations suggest shortening alone has little effect at matched mass; site density/exposure and the balance between elongation-driven monomer consumption and clearance control the response. Analysis includes 800 Latin-hypercube samples and modeled fibril lengths of 0.3–30 μm.
sections.unique_caveat: A mechanistic model, not direct measurement of fibril catalytic sites or patient biology; conclusions depend on assumptions about active-site creation, exposure and monomer clearance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; q-bio.SC primary category and a focused molecular mechanism with parameter-sweep evidence.

sections.title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
sections.abstract: Can structural representations improve venom-peptide ion-channel classification when entire taxa are held out?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine ESM-2 sequence embeddings with structure-aware graph networks and compare five structural priors on 1,373 ColabFold-predicted venom compounds from five taxa. In leave-one-taxon-out evaluation, persistent homology reaches 63.4% mean accuracy, versus about 54–55% for other geometric priors and about 30% for a sequence-only baseline; ordinary random splits mask the gap.
sections.unique_caveat: Computational evidence based on predicted structures and five taxa; no experimental binding/activity validation. The authors flag multi-label channel promiscuity and richer structural/dynamic modeling as future work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; cross-listed from cs.LG to q-bio.BM, with a taxon-held-out validation design.

sections.title: ProMORNA: An End-to-End Generative Framework for Full-Length mRNA Design
sections.abstract: Can a generative model design full-length mRNA candidates balancing predicted stability and translation?
sections.claimed_contribution: The v2 paper describes a BART-style model pretrained on over six million protein–mRNA pairs, then supervised fine-tuning and multi-objective reinforcement learning. The authors report in-silico Pareto-frontier gains and three independent in-vitro Fluc2P experiments: Candidate 2 had 3.33× the conventional benchmark’s 12–72 h reporter-activity AUC (Holm-adjusted P=0.01285); its estimated 1.29× advantage over the reported best GEMORNA candidate remained exploratory.
sections.unique_caveat: Reporter activity is not therapeutic efficacy, in-vivo performance or clinical evidence. The GEMORNA comparison is explicitly exploratory; this is a v2 revision of a May submission, not a new paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; substantive v2 update in the current batch, cross-listed across cs.LG, cs.AI and q-bio.BM, with three in-vitro assays.

sections.title: QProtFuse: Query-Guided Layer Fusion for Retrieval-Augmented Protein Function Prediction
sections.abstract: Can protein-language-model features from multiple layers improve query-conditioned retrieval for protein-function descriptions?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose query-guided fusion of protein-language-model layers with joint protein/annotation retrieval objectives. On Prot-Inst-OOD they report 16.4% Recall@1 with annotation reranking and improved LLM-as-judge scores for generated descriptions.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrieval and LLM-judge results are benchmark-specific and do not experimentally validate function. First submitted 2026-10-19; it appears as a q-bio.QM cross-list on 2026-10-23, not a new submission or versioned revision.

sections.title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
sections.abstract: Under what assumptions do positive trajectories in detailed-balanced mass-action systems converge to equilibrium?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors prove a unique positive equilibrium in each positive stoichiometric compatibility class and convergence of every positive trajectory, alongside a Lean 4 formalization using a persistence/barrier argument, the Horn–Jackson dissipation identity and bounded-speed descent.
sections.unique_caveat: A mathematical theorem under finite detailed-balanced mass-action assumptions, not empirical evidence for a particular biochemical network; application depends on those assumptions holding.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; cross-listed in q-bio.MN, math.DS and cs.LO, with a Lean 4 formalization noted in the arXiv comment.

sections.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure $^{64}$Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
sections.abstract: Can copper-64 be produced from natural zinc using a controlled D-D fusion neutron source?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors irradiated high-purity natural zinc for one hour and used gamma spectroscopy over 72 hours. They report no other copper radioisotope detected and threshold-corrected copper-64 purity estimates of 99.62% and 99.97% under two reporting thresholds.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not establish production yield, reproducible scale-up, full radiopharmaceutical manufacture or realized cost reduction; cost savings are prospective, not clinical outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; physics.med-ph paper with a direct radiopharmaceutical-production question and reported irradiation/spectroscopy.

sections.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
sections.abstract: Can physics-based simulated training pairs restore spatial detail in Cerenkov luminescence microscopy of tumor spheroids?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train CARE on 15,360 Monte-Carlo-generated image pairs from 80 simulated spheroid geometries. They report lower synthetic-validation MSE than Noise2Void (0.0051 vs 0.0492) and apply the model to experimental images from 27 U87 spheroids, reporting more localized signal and higher local contrast/SNR.
sections.unique_caveat: Quantitative ground truth is simulated; 27 spheroids are an experimental image set, not in-vivo or patient validation. Results depend on simulator fidelity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar Graph: 0 citations and 0 influential citations; direct imaging paper with simulation benchmarking and a 27-spheroid image application.

sections.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery

sections.title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic $ΔR_{1}$ and $ΔR_2^*$ sensing

sections.title: LieGROG: A Lie algebra approach for calibrating GRAPPA operators
sections.abstract: Can Lie-algebra calibration improve GRAPPA-operator gridding for non-Cartesian MRI?
sections.claimed_contribution: The author estimates a joint generator for GRAPPA operators and compares LieGROG with classical calibration and NUFFT/Toeplitz references across simulations and 2D/3D MR scans. sections.unique_caveat: This is reconstruction/compute benchmarking, not diagnostic accuracy or patient-outcome evidence. The arXiv comment says the work was submitted to Magnetic Resonance in Medicine, not accepted.

sections.title: Unified Projection-Domain Material Decomposition for Energy-Integrating and Photon-Counting CT
sections.abstract: Can one projection-domain decomposition method use multiple spectral measurements across different CT acquisition systems?
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors formulate nested optimization for two-material decomposition from at least two spectral measurements and test energy-integrating and photon-counting CT. They report noiseless line-integral errors below 3×10⁻⁶ g/cm² and noise within 3% of the Cramér–Rao bound; four rather than two photon-counting measurements reduce iodine CRLB by 19%.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is mainly simulation and comparison with vendor reconstructions, not improved diagnosis or patient outcomes; performance depends on tested scanner models and basis assumptions.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content:
**Molecular modeling and sequence-to-function tools.** RiboBridge, Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap, QProtFuse and the v2 ProMORNA report computational approaches spanning protein–RNA structure generation, cross-taxon peptide classification, protein-function retrieval and mRNA design. Evidence ranges from structural benchmarks to in-vitro reporter assays; these are not interchangeable levels of validation.

**Molecular mechanisms and formal models.** Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation and the tau/amyloid-β model use theoretical or simulation-based accounts of condensation and nucleation; Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems contributes a formal theorem rather than an experimental pathway study. This is modeling activity in the selected batch, not evidence of a field-wide shift.

**Medical imaging and treatment-planning methods.** AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy, the oxygen-enhanced MRI study, LieGROG, CT material decomposition and inverse planning address reconstruction, acquisition or optimization. Their evidence is simulation/phantom, small in-vitro/in-vivo pilot data or planning cases—not clinical benefit.

**Single-cell privacy is a focused result, not a recurring theme in this small batch.** The OneK1K benchmark shows why privacy auditing must include non-HVG handling as well as fidelity (2610.31454).

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content:
**Model-to-experiment validation.** RiboBridge reports complex-structure recovery on 124 benchmarks but not direct binding assays. Follow-up could synthesize a blinded subset of candidates, quantify affinity and specificity, and test whether predicted interface ranking tracks activity; this addresses the authors’ stated interface-ranking and sequence-realizability limits.

**Generalizable privacy evaluation.** The OneK1K study centers on one donor-split dataset and membership-inference metrics. A useful follow-up is a held-out-cohort comparison across tissues and platforms, with explicit privacy guarantees and attacks after the complete preprocessing/post-processing pipeline; distinguish formal guarantees from empirical attack resistance.

**Test molecular-model predictions.** The supercoiling and tau/amyloid papers make testable predictions about condensation barriers and active-site density. Experiments could vary DNA linking density and protein concentration while measuring droplet nucleation, then compare fibrils at matched mass with direct site-counting and secondary-nucleation assays. These are informed synthesis proposals, not established mechanisms.

**Validate imaging and delivery beyond proxies.** Cerenkov restoration should be tested on independent acquisition settings and reference structures; the oxygen-MRI pilot needs larger test–retest cohorts; hydrogel transport needs biological-barrier validation. CT decomposition and radiotherapy-planning methods need external-case or phantom-to-clinic validation before claims about patient outcomes.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This batch is notable for its mix of molecular-modeling papers and practical medical-physics methods, not measurable popularity: Semantic Scholar reported zero citations and zero influential citations for every selected paper at the snapshot. Evidence is mixed—mostly in-silico benchmarks, with a few in-vitro or small pilot experiments—and none alone establishes clinical effectiveness.
